messages.author: 67d9969f93ac5614
messages.subject: I do not want qplot to sort categorical x variable
parts:
Dear all,

SITUATION
x: categorical variable, values from {first, second, last}
y: quantitative variable.

QUESTION
qplot(x,y,data=myData) -> plots results in alphabetical order for x:
"first", "last", "second"
But I do not want this alphabetical ordering. I want the results to be
plotted in the order "first", "second", "last"
How to do this?

Thanks for your help!

Adi

messages.author: 67d9969f93ac5614
messages.subject: Re: I do not want qplot to sort categorical x variable
parts:
Dear all,

I found the answer to my problem. I had to change the data type of x
to "ordered" as follows:
x = ordered(x,levels=c("first","second","last").

Qplot respects this order, so my problem is solved!

Greetz,

Adi

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: I do not want qplot to sort categorical x variable
parts:
Dear Adi,

Ggplot does not change the order of your data. It uses the order from
the levels in your factor. Have a look at the examples below. Note that
the ordering in the second example comes from factor() and not from
ggplot.

library(ggplot2)
dataset <- data.frame(ABC = LETTERS[3:1], DEF = rnorm(3))
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = ABC, y = DEF)) + geom_point()
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = factor(ABC), y = DEF)) + geom_point()
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = factor(ABC, levels = c("B", "A", "C")), y =
DEF)) + geom_point()

HTH,

Thierry

messages.subject: Re: I do not want qplot to sort categorical x variable
parts:
Ista, 

It was something from last week that I linked. 

require(ggplot2)

levels(diamonds$color)
#[1] "D" "E" "F" "G" "H" "I" "J"

#colors sync'd with data correctly, but order of stack does not match legend
qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color)

#reverse levels of color
levels(diamonds$color)<-rev(levels(diamonds$color))

levels(diamonds$color)
#[1] "J" "I" "H" "G" "F" "E" "D"

#colors are out of order, but color names are in right order
qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color) 

#put the levels back
levels(diamonds$color)<-rev(levels(diamonds$color))

levels(diamonds$color)
#[1] "D" "E" "F" "G" "H" "I" "J"

#define breaks of scale_color_discrete() with reversed levels
qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color) + 
scale_fill_discrete(breaks = rev(levels(diamonds$color)))


My question is, why is it when you reverse the levels that the legend for scale_color_*() goes all wrong?  

That was my point.

I hope that is clear. 

Brandon

I think the problem is with your use of levels(). I never use it
myself, so I had to try it out:

> test <- factor(letters[1:10])
> test2 <- test
> levels(test2) <- rev(levels(test2))
> test3 <- factor(test, levels = rev(levels(test)))
>
> test
[1] a b c d e f g h i j
Levels: a b c d e f g h i j
> test2
[1] j i h g f e d c b a
Levels: j i h g f e d c b a
> test3
[1] a b c d e f g h i j
Levels: j i h g f e d c b a


It looks like levels() changes the actual values, rather than just the
order of the levels of a factor. So, back to your example: This works
for me as I would expect:


require(ggplot2)

data(diamonds)
print(qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color))

# reverse levels of color using factor() instead of levels()
diamonds$color<-factor(diamonds$color, levels=rev(levels(diamonds$color)))

levels(diamonds$color)
qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color)

messages.subject: Re: I do not want qplot to sort categorical x variable
parts:
Ista, 

The graph you made isn't as messed up as the one I made using levels(rev()), but it still isn't really what the original poster wanted. 

The color names (D,E,F) are stacked in the right order (top to bottom), but the bars on the graph are stacked in reverse order. Look at the colors and letters. On the first graph D is "salmon" and E is "mustard," and they are on the bottom. On the second graph, D is "pink" and E is "lavendar" and they are at the top. 

It seems that it plots the bars in the order of the factor (bottom to top), but then when it plots the legend it puts them from top to bottom. 

Is this only an issue with stacked barplots? 

Brandon

P.S. It seems I may have had my levels() reversed when I started saving the graphs so my original in the last email is the screwed up one and the reversed one is the right one to start with. :/

parts: Hi Brandon,

On Thu, Sep 9, 2010 at 10:56 AM, Brandon Hurr <bhi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Ista,
> The graph you made isn't as messed up as the one I made using levels(rev()),
> but it still isn't really what the original poster wanted.

I assume you are talking about the OP of this thread:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/5e4cb9d6d3b36b2f/31f69c8fc32f2558
rather than the current one.

> The color names (D,E,F) are stacked in the right order (top to bottom), but
> the bars on the graph are stacked in reverse order. Look at the colors and
> letters. On the first graph D is "salmon" and E is "mustard," and they are
> on the bottom. On the second graph, D is "pink" and E is "lavendar" and they
> are at the top.
> It seems that it plots the bars in the order of the factor (bottom to top),
> but then when it plots the legend it puts them from top to bottom.

Right. So the _only_ issue I see is that some people would like to
have legends ordered from bottom to top instead of top to bottom. I'm
not saying I disagree with that, I'm just trying to clear away the
noise about "reordering factors doesn't work for color scales" or
"doesn't work for plot colors". Those are non-issues, because it does
work, provided that you reorder the levels of your factors correctly.

Furthermore, we have already established that you can change the order
in which the legend is printed using the breaks argument to your color
scale. So this all boils down to "hey Hadley, can you change the
default legend order so that it is ordered from bottom to top instead
of top to bottom?". I think that might make some sense, but then again
I can see arguments against it. I think most people read legends
starting at the top and visually scanning down, so ordering from the
top down also makes sense. Further, if you dodge the bars instead of
stacking them then the default ordering makes more sense: try

qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color, position="dodge")

and notice that the legend colors read from top to bottom match the
plot colors from left to right. Since left-right top-bottom is a
natural order in which western people tend to scan a page, that makes
a lot of sense to me. So now maybe we ask "hey Hadley, can you change
the default legend order so that it is ordered from bottom to top
instead of top to bottom, but only if position = 'stacked' ?".
Personally I'm fine with manually changing the order using the breaks
argument if I need to.

Sorry this turned into a rant I'm afraid...

Best wishes all,
Ista

> Brandon
